international.title: Qantas and Air New Zealand planes too close at Sydney airport as ‘mental models’ of flight crews to be investigated
international.summary: Aborted descent on Wednesday morning is latest in a series of landing incidents at Sydney airport Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The Australian Transport Safety Bureau is investigating flight crews’ “mental models” after a Qantas plane aborted its landing at Sydney airport on Wednesday after noticing another aircraft crossing the runway while on its descent. The ATSB said Qantas flight 426 from Melbourne was due to land just before 10.15am on Wednesday, with the Boeing 737 jet told to expect a late landing clearance due to aircraft crossing the runway.
